title: “Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, PM Modi Ke Saath” to be Organised Nationwide on 27th August 2026 to celebrate National Sports Day
subtitle:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi to Address Young Budding Athletes on Sports, Youth Leadership and Viksit Bharat
Dialogue to bring Youth, Athletes and Policymakers Together Across 1,500+ Educational Institutions
body_text:
To celebrate the National Sports Day 2026, the nation is set to witness a large-scale youth engagement initiative, “Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, Pradhan Mantri Modi Ke Saath”, on 27 August 2026, bringing together young people, athletes and educational institutions at more than 1,500 locations across the country.
The nationwide initiative will create a direct platform for young budding athletes to share their ideas, suggestions and innovative thoughts on the future of India’s sports and youth ecosystem. IITs, IIMs, NITs, AIIMS, leading medical colleges and universities will be among the educational institutions participating in the programme.
The programme will feature a virtual address by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Following the Prime Minister’s address, physical programmes will commence simultaneously across the participating locations.
The programme seeks to strengthen the connection between the aspirations and ground-level experiences of young people and policymaking. Youth participants will engage around four key themes: strengthening the sports ecosystem and expanding grassroots facilities, coaching and opportunities; nurturing talent for the 2036 Olympics through scientific talent identification and athlete development; enhancing youth leadership and participation in governance; and empowering young people with future-ready skills, volunteering and nation-building opportunities.
A major feature of the initiative will be direct interaction between youth having interest in sports and leading Indian athletes and medal winners. Prominent sportspersons including Deepa Karmakar, Saina Nehwal, Gagan Narang, Sreejesh, Mary Kom, Baichung Bhutia, Gopichand, Anju Bobby George, Karnam Malleswari, Mirabai Chanu and P.T. Usha, along with prominent cricketers, will engage with youth and share their sporting journeys, challenges, and experiences.
The participation will extend beyond athletes, with Members of Parliament, Members of Legislative Assemblies, Union Ministers, Ministers of State and State Sports Ministers engaging with young people and seeking their ideas and suggestions on the four identified themes.
The initiative will also feature the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue Quiz and encourage young participants to register on the MY Bharat Portal, creating an avenue for sustained youth engagement beyond the one-day programme.
“Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, Pradhan Mantri Modi Ke Saath” seeks to reinforce the idea that India’s sporting transformation is ultimately powered by its young people. By bringing youth aspirations, sporting experiences and policy perspectives onto a common platform, the initiative aims to give youth a meaningful voice in shaping the future of sports and youth development in the country.
*****
Pawan Singh Faujdar / Ayushman Kumar

ministry.name: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports announced a nationwide event, "Khelo India Dialogue – Khel Ki Baat, Pradhan Mantri Modi Ke Saath," to be held on 27 August 2026 to mark National Sports Day, involving over 1,500 educational institutions. PM Narendra Modi will give a virtual address to young athletes, followed by interactions involving prominent sportspersons, MPs, MLAs and ministers around four themes including grassroots sports infrastructure, 2036 Olympics preparation, youth leadership, and future-ready skills. The event also includes a quiz and encourages registration on the MY Bharat Portal for sustained youth engagement.
enrichment.context: National Sports Day is observed on 29 August each year to mark the birth anniversary of hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand, and is typically used by the government to launch or highlight youth and sports-related initiatives under the broader Khelo India umbrella scheme, which aims to promote grassroots sports development and identify talent for international competitions. This event ties into India's stated ambition to bid for or prepare for hosting the 2036 Olympics, a goal the government has referenced in various sports policy contexts. The MY Bharat Portal is a government platform for youth volunteering and civic engagement, reflecting the administration's push to formalize youth participation in governance and nation-building narratives.
